# SK7093 — The console is written to where a logger was meant

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `Console.Write` or `Console.WriteLine` is made from code that has a logger in scope.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S106 |

## Why

A console write cannot be filtered, routed, structured or correlated, and in every hosted environment — a container, a service, a function, a test host — it goes nowhere anybody looks. Complements `SK2016`, which assumes a logger is being used at all.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
public Importer(ILogger<Importer> logger) => this.logger = logger;

public void Import(string path) {
    Console.WriteLine($"importing {path}");
}
```

Write:

```csharp
public void Import(string path) {
    logger.LogInformation("importing {Path}", path);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The rule does not decide whether this code is an application or a library, because nothing in the tree can tell it.** `LooseLoader` builds its compilation as `OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary`, so "this is a library" and "no project file was loaded" are one observation, and loose is the mode Skala exists for. A rule keyed on `OutputKind` would report every line of every console application analysed without its project, which is `S106` turned into a false-positive engine. What ships is the narrower fact the issue's own title names and which no load mode can distort: **a logger is in scope at this call site and the code wrote to the console anyway** — a member or parameter typed `ILogger`, `ILogger<T>` or `ILog` is present, so the routing question is already answered for this code and answered differently two lines away. That is a contradiction inside one method rather than a policy judgement about the project. A console application's entry point printing usage has no logger and is never reported, which is the correct outcome by construction rather than by an exemption somebody has to maintain — and a service class that writes to the console and has no logger at all is under-reported, deliberately. The logger interface is matched on the type's own name and not on a namespace, because the namespace is the part that differs across `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, `Serilog`, `NLog` and `log4net`. `Console.Out` and `Console.Error` are reported through the receiver, so a `TextWriter` the caller handed in is not the console and never fires; reads such as `Console.ReadLine` never fire. Report-only: which level the line deserves is intent — `Debug`, `Information` and `Error` are all plausible for the same string — a console argument list is not mechanically a message template, and an edit that guessed would put the wrong severity on somebody's alerting.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7093.severity`
